title: No __main__ guard: importing the module runs the full 6-run experiment and downloads/materializes datasets at import time
description: The RUN block executes at module top level: 'for seed in SEEDS: for condition in CONDITIONS: run_one_seed(...)'. There is no 'if __name__ == "__main__"' guard. Datasets are downloaded/materialized (109-180) and output directories created (41-42) at import. Any 'import m7_trimodal_run', static tool, or test collection therefore starts a 4-5 hour training run and a multi-GB download.
evidence: lines 707-711 at module scope: 'all_results = []' then 'for seed in SEEDS: for condition in CONDITIONS: result = run_one_seed(seed, condition)'; dataset loaders 119-179; 'for d in [...]: d.mkdir(...)' 41-42
fix: Move dataset loading, directory creation and the seed/condition loop into a main() guarded by 'if __name__ == "__main__": main()'. The provenance sibling already does this and can be mirrored.

title: Replay sample() filters TASK ids against a CLASS-keyed store and draws <=1 embedding per class
description: _store is keyed by class label (0-19), but callers pass replay_task_ids=[1] (T2) and [1,2] (T3) meaning TASK numbers. sample() computes 'available = [c for c in task_ids if c in self._store]', so it keeps only the class(es) whose integer label equals a task id: T2 replay uses only class 1, T3 replay uses only classes 1 and 2. It then draws exactly one embedding per selected class, so a requested replay_batch of 32 yields at most 1-2 samples. self._task_labels (the map that would make this correct) is never consulted.
evidence: line 383 'available = [c for c in task_ids if c in self._store]'; line 386 'np.random.choice(available, size=min(batch_size, len(available)), replace=False)'; lines 388-391 one 'idx = np.random.randint(len(self._store[c]))' per class; callers 569 (task_ids=[1]) and 596 ([1,2])
fix: Select classes via _task_labels (classes whose task id is requested) and sample multiple embeddings per class up to batch_size, instead of one per class. Cloned in the provenance sibling.

title: populate() uses label_offset=0 for every task, so SHD classes overwrite N-MNIST in the class-keyed store
description: _store is keyed by 'c = int(lbl.item()) + label_offset' and populate() is called with label_offset=0 for T1 (nmnist, classes 0-9) and T2 (shd, classes 0-19). SHD classes 0-9 overwrite the stored N-MNIST embeddings under the same keys. By T3, replay 'of T1 and T2' contains no N-MNIST embeddings at all, so T1 gets zero replay protection during T3. Combined with RUN-002 the replay signal is both misrouted and largely destroyed.
evidence: line 369 'c = int(lbl.item()) + label_offset'; call sites line 553 '...task_id=1, label_offset=0' and line 584 '...task_id=2, label_offset=0'
fix: Key the store so class collisions across tasks are impossible (e.g. by (task_id, class) or a per-task offset) and make sample() task-aware (RUN-002). A real per-task label_offset is the minimal fix. Cloned in the provenance sibling.

title: Replayed embeddings pass through the CURRENT task head, not the originating task head
description: During task T, replay is scored via 'forward_from_embeddings(replay_embs, task_name)' where task_name is the current task. Old-task embeddings are pushed through the current head and trained against old-class integer labels. This does nothing to preserve the previous task's head (the purpose of rehearsal) and instead trains the current head on foreign-class targets. forward_from_embeddings has no way to select the originating head.
evidence: line 453 'replay_logits = self.model.forward_from_embeddings(replay_embs, task_name)'; def 344-349 uses 'self.heads[task_name]'
fix: Store the originating task per embedding (RUN-030) and route each replayed embedding through its own head; forward_from_embeddings must accept a per-group task identity. Cloned in the provenance sibling.

title: 'fwt' is T2 learning gain (after minus zero-shot), mislabeled as forward transfer
description: fwt = acc_t2_after_t2 - acc_t2_zero_shot measures how much SHD improved by training on SHD; it is a learning gain, not forward transfer. The zero-shot baseline (559) evaluates SHD through a randomly initialized SHD backbone and head, so it is near chance and 'fwt' is essentially SHD test accuracy minus chance. Reporting this as 'forward transfer ~75 pp' overstates a transfer effect the quantity does not measure. The provenance sibling keeps 'learning_gain' and 'fwt' as separate quantities and defines fwt against a random-init baseline.
evidence: line 616 'fwt = acc_t2_after_t2 - acc_t2_zero_shot'; line 559 zero-shot eval; contrast provenance 1065-1066 which separates learning_gain_t2 from fwt_t2
fix: Rename this field to learning_gain (or gain_T2); if a forward-transfer number is needed, define it against a from-scratch/random-init baseline as the provenance sibling does. Do not let downstream docs call this 'forward transfer'.

title: 'forgetting_T1_T3' is the incremental T2->T3 delta, not total T1 forgetting after T3
description: forgetting_t1_t3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 measures only the additional T1 drop during T3 training. Its sibling metrics use start-to-end semantics: forgetting_T1_T2 = acc_t1 - acc_t1_after_t2 and forgetting_T2_T3 = acc_t2_after_t2 - acc_t2_after_t3. Under a name that reads as 'T1 forgetting measured after T3', a reader expects acc_t1 - acc_t1_after_t3. The inconsistent definition will be misread when aggregated.
evidence: line 614 'forgetting_t1_t3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3' stored as 'forgetting_T1_T3' at 628; compare 613 (T1_T2 total) and 615 (T2_T3 total)
fix: Rename to forgetting_T1_incremental_T3, or redefine as acc_t1 - acc_t1_after_t3 to match the total-forgetting semantics of the other two fields; document which is intended.

title: Reported test accuracy uses last-epoch weights; the best-val checkpoint is saved but never reloaded
description: train_task saves best_*.pt whenever val improves (485-495) but never reloads it. test_acc is computed on whatever weights exist after the loop (504, last or early-stopped epoch), and the caller saves final_*.pt from that same last-epoch state (543/571/598). Early stopping thus governs when training halts, but the model carried forward and reported is the last-epoch model, not the best-val model. best_*.pt is dead output.
evidence: lines 485-495 save 'best_{task_name}_{modality}.pt'; line 504 'test_acc = self.evaluate(test_loader, ...)' after the loop; caller torch.save of final_*.pt at 543/571/598; no torch.load of best_*.pt anywhere
fix: Either load best_*.pt before the final test eval and before saving final_*.pt, or drop the best-checkpoint machinery and state that reporting is last-epoch. Decide deliberately and document it.

title: best_*.pt filename omits seed and condition, so all 6 runs overwrite the same 3 files
description: The best-checkpoint path is 'best_{task_name}_{modality}.pt' with no seed or condition. Across 3 seeds x 2 conditions the loop writes only best_nmnist_nmnist.pt, best_shd_shd.pt, best_dvs_dvs.pt, so every run clobbers the previous run's best checkpoint. (final_*.pt is correctly namespaced by seed and condition at 536/562/589.) Even ignoring RUN-007, no per-run best weights survive, which also violates the repo's back-up-every-seed rule.
evidence: line 488 'ckpt_path = CKPT_DIR / f"best_{task_name}_{modality}.pt"' vs final path line 536 'final_nmnist_nmnist_seed{seed}_{condition}.pt'
fix: Include seed and condition (and ideally step) in the best_*.pt filename, matching the final_*.pt convention.

title: Silent checkpoint-skip loads stale final_*.pt with no provenance check and skips gate-trajectory logging
description: For each task, if final_{task}_{task}_seed{seed}_{condition}.pt exists the code loads it and skips training (prints only a skip glyph). There is no check that the checkpoint matches current code/config, so a stale checkpoint yields stale results presented as fresh. Because _save_gate_history is only called in the training branch (544/572/599), a skipped task writes no gate trajectory, so gate_trajectory.csv under-populates or is empty on any reuse run - and that CSV is the sole source for the paper's core gate-specialization figure.
evidence: lines 537-539 'if ckpt_t1.exists(): ... model.load_state_dict(torch.load(...))'; repeated 563-565 and 590-592; _save_gate_history only inside the else branch at 544/572/599
fix: Record code/config version with each checkpoint and refuse or warn on mismatch; regenerate/reload the gate trajectory on skip so gate_trajectory.csv is never silently partial. At minimum fail loudly instead of skipping silently.

title: Results CSV mixes two schemas and appends via read-concat-overwrite with no dedup
description: cl_trimodal_results.csv receives end-of-seed summary rows (no 'step' key, 618-640) and per-task incremental rows (with a 'step' key, 687-697) in one file. Both writers do read-concat-write with no de-duplication, so re-running any seed appends duplicate rows that silently inflate n and corrupt mean/std. The only discriminator between the schemas is presence of 'step', so the mandatory 'df[df.step.isna()].drop_duplicates()' ritual is load-bearing and fragile. gate_trajectory.csv (650-684) has the same append-without-dedup pattern.
evidence: summary write 635-640 'df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame([result])])' (result has no 'step'); incremental write 690-696 with a row containing 'step'; gate write 681-683 same concat pattern
fix: Write a single normalized schema (or one file per schema), key rows by (seed, condition, step), and upsert on that key instead of blind append; or centralize on the canonical loader and never append raw. Document the schema.

title: Accuracy is recorded and reported with no spike-rate/sparsity or timestep cost
description: This is an SNN paper, yet evaluate() returns only accuracy and the saved result dict contains only accuracies, forgetting and fwt (618-631). The forward pass produces spike counts (backbone sums over T) but spike rate/sparsity is never computed, logged, or written to any CSV, and the timestep counts (25 visual, 100 SHD) are not recorded either. The repo rule requires accuracy to travel with spike rate/sparsity and timestep count, so every accuracy this script emits is incomplete as a reported result.
evidence: lines 417-419 evaluate returns '100.0 * correct / total'; result dict 618-631 has no spike-rate/sparsity/timestep fields; no spike-rate computation anywhere in the file
fix: Instrument the forward pass to accumulate mean spike rate/sparsity per layer and add spike-rate/sparsity and per-modality timestep columns to the results CSV so every accuracy is reported with its cost.

title: HGRN reset gate is inert: h_prev is always zero, so r*h_prev is 0 and W_r/norm_r get no gradient
description: ImprovedHGRNGate is only ever called with a single argument (self.hgrn(features) at 340, self.hgrn(embs) at 347), so h_prev defaults to zeros on every call and the gate is never used recurrently. With h_prev=0, 'r * h_prev' is identically 0, h_tilde reduces to tanh(norm_h(W_h([x,0]))) and the output is 'z * h_tilde'. The reset gate r (and W_r, norm_r) has zero effect on the output and receives zero gradient, so those parameters stay at init. The multiplicative reset r*h_prev is exactly the operation flagged as the central SpiNNaker risk (R3) and a novelty of the paper - and in the model as run it does nothing.
evidence: line 226 'h_prev = torch.zeros(batch_size, ...)'; line 230 'h_tilde = torch.tanh(self.norm_h(self.W_h(torch.cat([x, r * h_prev], dim=-1))))'; line 231 'return (1 - z) * h_prev + z * h_tilde'; call sites 340 and 347 pass no h_prev
fix: Decide what the HGRN should do: if recurrence is intended, thread a real hidden state; if not, remove the reset gate and its weights and revise the novelty/SpiNNaker-R3 claims. Either way it must not be described as a working multiplicative-reset recurrent gate.

title: Near-zero forgetting is structural: only hopfield/hgrn/gate are shared across tasks; backbones and heads are grad-isolated
description: Each task has its own backbone (keyed by task name) and its own head, and the optimizer only updates parameters in the current task's forward graph, so an inactive task's backbone/head receive no gradient and are effectively frozen. The only parameters shared and trainable across all three tasks are the Hopfield layer, the HGRN gate, and the adaptive gate. Any measured forgetting can only come from drift in those three modules, so near-zero forgetting is largely a consequence of architectural isolation, not of replay. Summaries must not attribute the ~0 pp forgetting to replay preventing catastrophic forgetting.
evidence: per-task backbones 277-292 and per-task heads 298-300; optimizer over all params 424 but forward/replay only touch current-task modules; T1 re-eval after T2/T3 (580, 607) uses the unchanged nmnist backbone/head plus drifted shared modules
fix: No code change required for correctness, but reporting must state that forgetting is measured only through the shared hopfield/hgrn/gate modules and is bounded by architectural isolation; keep the claim to 'replay enables gate specialization' per repo RULE 5.

title: SHD runs at 100 timesteps while N-MNIST/DVS run at 25; CONFIG['time_steps'] is ignored
description: events_to_dense hardcodes time_bins=100, so SHD sequences are 100 steps, whereas the N-MNIST and DVS collate functions hardcode 25 steps. CONFIG['time_steps']=25 is never read by any path. Timestep count is a first-order SNN cost and accuracy determinant, it differs across modalities, and it is not recorded with results (see RUN-011).
evidence: line 139 'time_bins, channels = 100, 700'; nmnist collate 77-80 and dvs collate 94-97 use 25; CONFIG['time_steps'] set at 58 and never read
fix: Derive all timestep counts from a single config value (or explicitly document the intended per-modality T) and record the timestep count in the results CSV.

title: Collate truncates every sample to the first 25 frames, discarding most of each recording
description: Both nmnist_collate_fn and dvs_collate_fn keep only e[:25] frames and zero-pad shorter ones. With ToFrame time_windows of 1000 us for N-MNIST (117) and 50000 us for DVS (165), each raw recording produces many more than 25 frames, so the truncation silently drops the later part of every sample. The retained window is fixed by a magic 25 rather than derived from CONFIG['time_steps']. This is a modeling decision that materially affects both accuracy and spike cost and is undocumented.
evidence: line 78 'e = e[:25]' (nmnist); line 95 'e = e[:25]' (dvs); ToFrame time_window=1000 at 117 and 50000 at 165
fix: Choose the ToFrame time_window and the kept-frame count together so the 25 frames cover the intended fraction of each recording, source the count from config, and document the temporal coverage per modality.

title: SupervisedContrastiveLoss includes the self/diagonal term in both the positive mask and the denominator
description: The positive mask is 'labels==labels' which is 1 on the diagonal, and the log-prob denominator sums over all j including j==i, with no logits_mask to remove self-contrast. Standard SupCon (Khosla et al.) excludes the anchor itself from both positives and denominator. Including self gives every anchor a trivial always-satisfied positive (its own normalized similarity, the largest term after max-subtraction), diluting the contrastive gradient and biasing the loss, most visibly for classes appearing once per batch.
evidence: line 193 'mask = torch.eq(labels.unsqueeze(1), labels.unsqueeze(0)).float()'; lines 196-198 build exp_logits and mean_log_prob without masking the diagonal
fix: Build a logits_mask that removes self from the denominator and from mask before the mean, matching the canonical SupCon formulation; this will move the loss and thus results, so flag it as a deliberate numeric change.

title: Entire SHD train+test set is densified into a Python list of [100,1,1,700] tensors at import
description: shd_train_data and shd_test_data are built by list comprehensions that convert every SHD sample to a dense [100,700] float tensor (unsqueezed to [100,1,1,700]) and hold them all in memory before training. events_to_dense also fills the dense tensor with a per-event Python for-loop (145-147) rather than vectorized indexing. This is eager full-dataset materialization at import (compounding RUN-001) and is both memory-heavy and slow.
evidence: lines 149-150 'shd_train_data = [events_to_dense(e, l) for e, l in tqdm(shd_train...)]' and same for shd_test; per-event loop 145-147
fix: Densify lazily inside a Dataset/transform (as N-MNIST and DVS do via tonic) or cache to disk, and vectorize the t/x index assignment instead of the Python loop.

title: Backbone fc1=Linear(64*5*5,1024) hardcodes a 34x34 input, forcing DVS to be pooled to 34x34 in collate
description: SNN_Backbone.fc1 assumes the post-conv spatial size that results only from a 34x34 input (conv5->30, pool->15, conv5->11, pool->5 => 64*5*5=1600). To satisfy this fixed fan-in, dvs_collate_fn adaptively pools native 128x128 DVS frames down to 34x34 (98-102), a large downsampling for a visual-motion task. The coupling is implicit: no assertion, nothing derives the fan-in from input size, so any input-resolution change silently breaks the layer. (This 1600x1024 fan-in is also the basis of the SpiNNaker core budget.)
evidence: line 242 'self.fc1 = nn.Linear(64 * 5 * 5, 1024)'; dvs collate pooling to (34,34) at lines 98-102
fix: Derive the conv output size dynamically (lazy linear or a shape probe) or assert the expected input size; document why DVS is pooled to 34x34 and the information loss it implies.

title: Determinism only partially configured: torch+numpy global seeds set, but not deterministic algorithms or per-loader RNG
description: run_one_seed sets torch.manual_seed(seed) and np.random.seed(seed) only. It does not call torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True), does not configure MPS/CUDA determinism, and does not pin the shuffle generator of the module-level train DataLoaders (created once at import with shuffle=True and no generator). Reproducibility therefore depends on exact global-RNG consumption order across the six sequential runs sharing those loaders, which is fragile. (Python's 'random' is not imported, so that gap is moot.)
evidence: lines 523-524 'torch.manual_seed(seed)' and 'np.random.seed(seed)'; train loaders 127/155/173 use shuffle=True with no generator
fix: Set torch.use_deterministic_algorithms where supported, pass an explicitly seeded generator to each training DataLoader, and document the MPS determinism caveat so seed-to-seed variation is attributable.

title: Real training uses hardcoded 15 epochs / patience 5 / lr 1e-3 / wd 1e-4, overriding CONFIG and the defaults
description: train_task defaults to num_epochs=50, patience=12, lr=1e-3 and hardcodes weight_decay=1e-4 in the optimizer, but every call site passes num_epochs=15 and patience=5 (542, 567-570, 594-597). CONFIG['max_epochs']=50 and CONFIG['patience']=12 are therefore never used and disagree with the actual run, and weight_decay ignores CONFIG['weight_decay']. Anyone reading CONFIG or the signature to learn the training budget gets the wrong numbers.
evidence: line 422 defaults 'num_epochs=50, patience=12, lr=1e-3'; line 424 'weight_decay=1e-4'; call sites 542, 567-570, 594-597 pass num_epochs=15, patience=5
fix: Single-source the schedule from CONFIG (max_epochs, patience, learning_rate, weight_decay) and pass those values at the call sites; remove the divergent literals.

title: 14 of 19 CONFIG keys are never read, implying configurability the code does not have
description: Only batch_size, gradient_clip, beta, num_patterns and contrastive_temperature are read. The other keys - learning_rate, weight_decay, max_epochs, patience, dropout, hidden_dim, num_gru_layers, num_workers, time_steps, pin_memory, use_contrastive, contrastive_weight, seed, device - are never consumed; their behaviors are hardcoded elsewhere (RUN-014, RUN-020) or absent (dropout, num_gru_layers). This is misleading: it looks tunable but most knobs do nothing.
evidence: CONFIG dict 45-65; read keys at 46->127, 51->457, 52->238, 55->293, 61->427; the remaining keys have no read site in the file
fix: Delete the unused keys or wire them into the code they claim to control; keep CONFIG as the single source of truth for anything it lists.

title: Backbone fc3/lif5 (visual) and fc4/lif4 (audio) are dead: their outputs are always discarded
description: SNN_Backbone.fc3/lif5 produce spk5, but both callers take only the second return ('_, features = bb(x)' at 305 and 324), so spk5 is computed for all 25 timesteps every forward and thrown away. In the audio backbone, fc4/lif4 are never referenced by the audio unroll (which stops at fc3/lif3), so they are pure dead parameters. These are vestigial standalone classifier heads left from before per-task self.heads took over.
evidence: line 246 'self.fc3 = nn.Linear(512, num_classes)'; 268-270 compute f3/s5/spk5_rec; consumers '_, features = bb(x)' at 305 and 324; audio fc4/lif4 288-289 unused by 312-318/331-336
fix: Remove fc3/lif5 and the spk5 accumulation from SNN_Backbone (and fc4/lif4 from the audio backbone), or if kept for standalone use document that M7 does not use them; this also trims per-timestep compute.

title: _get_features and forward duplicate the whole backbone feature-extraction, including the audio unroll verbatim
description: The audio-backbone temporal unroll in _get_features (307-318) is a verbatim copy of the same block in forward (326-337), and the visual branch '_, features = bb(x)' is duplicated too. Any change to feature extraction (e.g. adding spike-rate logging per RUN-011, or fixing timesteps per RUN-014) must be made in two places, which is exactly how numeric drift between the replay path and the training path is introduced.
evidence: lines 302-319 (_get_features) vs 321-342 (forward) contain the same isinstance branch and audio for-loop
fix: Extract a single _extract_features(x, modality) helper and call it from both _get_features and forward.

title: safe_empty_cache is never called and ignores MPS despite its 'MPS/CPU compatibility' banner
description: The function only empties the CUDA cache and sits under a 'MPS/CPU compatibility helpers' header, but it has no MPS branch (torch.mps.empty_cache) and is never called anywhere in the file. Dead code.
evidence: lines 20-22 def safe_empty_cache with only 'if torch.cuda.is_available(): torch.cuda.empty_cache()'; no call site
fix: Remove it, or if MPS memory pressure is real, call it at task boundaries and add a torch.mps.empty_cache branch.

title: Unused stdlib imports os, sys, time
description: os, sys and time are imported at the top of the file but never used anywhere in it.
evidence: lines 4-6 'import os', 'import sys', 'import time'; no references elsewhere
fix: Remove the three unused imports.

title: Dead local import 'from torch.nn import Linear, LayerNorm' inside the model constructor
description: Inside the tasks loop the constructor does 'from torch.nn import Linear, LayerNorm', but the code below builds modules with nn.Linear / nn.LayerNorm and never uses the bare Linear or LayerNorm names. The import is dead and runs once per audio task.
evidence: line 280 'from torch.nn import Linear, LayerNorm'; subsequent code uses nn.Linear (282-288)
fix: Remove the local import.

title: pandas imported mid-file at line 648, after the functions that use it are defined
description: run_one_seed (521-643) and the two CSV helpers reference pd, but 'import pandas as pd' appears at line 648. It works only because those functions are first called at line 710, after the import executes; calling run_one_seed before line 648 would raise NameError. A latent trap that also hides a heavy dependency mid-module.
evidence: line 648 'import pandas as pd'; pd first referenced at 636 inside run_one_seed defined at 521
fix: Move 'import pandas as pd' to the top-of-file import block with the other imports.

title: ModernHopfieldLayer default num_patterns=256 is dead, and it has two redundant scaling knobs
description: The constructor default num_patterns=256 is never used because the call site passes CONFIG['num_patterns']=100 (293); reading the signature alone wrongly suggests 256 (a known repo trap). Separately, forward divides by both self.temperature (fixed 1.0) and self.scale=sqrt(dim), two scaling factors where modern Hopfield normally uses a single inverse-temperature beta; with temperature=1.0 one is a no-op and the pair is confusing.
evidence: line 202 'def __init__(self, dim=512, num_patterns=256, temperature=1.0)'; call site 293 passes CONFIG['num_patterns']=100; line 206 'self.scale = np.sqrt(dim)'; line 209 '/ self.temperature / self.scale'
fix: Set the constructor default to the intended 100 (or remove the default), and collapse the two scaling factors into one documented beta.

title: Model moved to device twice and device passed as a string rather than torch.device
description: The model is moved with .to(device) at creation (529) and again inside ContinualLearner.__init__ (402). The buffer and trainer are constructed with str(device) (530-531), so self.device is the string 'mps'/'cpu' rather than a torch.device, inconsistent with the module-level torch.device object and with populate() which uses next(model.parameters()).device. It works but is redundant and type-inconsistent.
evidence: line 529 'model = M7_ContinualAdaptiveModel(...).to(device)'; line 402 'self.model = model.to(device)'; lines 530-531 'device=str(device)'
fix: Move the model once and pass the torch.device object (not str) consistently to the buffer and trainer.

title: _task_labels is populated but never read - the exact map needed to fix the replay bugs
description: EmbeddingReplayBuffer records self._task_labels[c] = task_id in populate (378) but nothing ever reads _task_labels. This is the per-class task identity that sample() (RUN-002) and forward_from_embeddings routing (RUN-004) need to be correct; it is computed and then ignored.
evidence: line 359 'self._task_labels = {}'; line 378 'self._task_labels[c] = task_id'; no read of _task_labels anywhere
fix: Consume _task_labels in sample() to select by task, and carry it through to route replay embeddings to the correct head (see RUN-002, RUN-004).

title: Stale comment claims the caller renames the final checkpoint; no rename exists
description: The comment 'Save final checkpoint (caller handles condition suffix via rename after return)' describes a rename that never happens - the caller writes a fresh final_*.pt via torch.save (543/571/598) and no code renames anything. The comment misleads a reader about the checkpoint flow.
evidence: line 502 comment; caller torch.save at 543, 571, 598; no os.rename/Path.rename in the file
fix: Delete or correct the comment to reflect that the caller writes final_*.pt directly.

title: PLOT_DIR is created at import but never used
description: PLOT_DIR is defined and mkdir'd at import but nothing in the file writes to it (figures are generated by a separate script). It is dead, and its creation is part of the import-time side effects.
evidence: line 40 'PLOT_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "plots"'; line 41 mkdir loop; no other reference to PLOT_DIR
fix: Remove PLOT_DIR (and its mkdir) from this file, or move directory creation into the guarded main().

title: events_to_dense: binary occupancy, redundant max_time guard, and divide-by-zero when all timestamps are equal
description: The dense encoding sets dense[t,c]=1.0, so repeated events at the same (t,c) do not accumulate (occupancy, not count). max_time is guarded by 'if len(events)>0 else 1' but the real risk is max_time==0 (all events at t=0), which makes 'events[t]/max_time' divide by zero and yields invalid indices after astype(int). The guard checks length, not max_time.
evidence: line 142 'max_time = events["t"].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1'; line 143 divides by max_time; line 147 'dense[t, c] = 1.0'
fix: Guard max_time with 'max(events["t"].max(), 1)', and decide deliberately between occupancy and event-count encoding.

title: Train/val split generator is fixed at manual_seed(42) independent of the experiment seed
description: All three random_split calls use torch.Generator().manual_seed(42), so the train/val partition is identical across experiment seeds 42/123/456 - only model init and DataLoader shuffling vary. This is the documented intent (splits fixed across seeds), recorded here so it is not mistaken for a bug or 'fixed' by wiring in the run seed.
evidence: lines 126, 154, 172 'generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(42)'
fix: No change needed; keep as-is and document that the split is intentionally seed-independent.

title: Derived metrics survive only in the end-of-seed summary row; an interrupted seed loses forgetting/fwt
description: Only the raw T*_after_T* accuracies are persisted incrementally after each task (549/577/604). All derived metrics (forgetting_T1_T2, forgetting_T1_T3, forgetting_T2_T3, fwt) are computed and written only in the final summary row (612-640). If a seed is interrupted after some tasks, the incremental rows remain but no derived metrics are recoverable, and the checkpoints alone do not contain them.
evidence: incremental saves 549, 577, 604 store only accuracies; derived metrics computed 613-616 and saved only in the summary row 618-640
fix: Persist derived metrics incrementally as they become computable (e.g. after T2 write forgetting_T1_T2 and fwt) so an interrupted run is analyzable.
